messages:
Maya: heads up — spotted a latency spike on flashv3 for a narrow head-dim slice, digging in :eyes:
Sam: which head dims and seq lens?
Maya: mostly head_dim=22 and 30 on causal requests with seq_len around 480-520. pattern: flashv3 selected, then 80ms later it falls back to sdpa/v2 path and overall p95 jumps.
Toni: that sounds like the bucketizer flipping kernels mid-request due to KV cache warmup? :thinking:
Maya: maybe. here is a tiny excerpt from the perf log: 
```
seq_len=502 head_dim=22 causal=true microbatch=1
kernel_probe=flashv3 chosen
kv_cache_hit_ratio=0.12
after_kv_warmup=60ms fallback=sdpa_v2 slowpath
end
```
Sam: ah, kv_cache_hit_ratio is low so the runtime re-evaluates batching/kernel choice after first tokens. our heuristic currently recomputes kernel pick when effective_seqlen changes > 64, but it ignores head_dim interplay.
Liam: can reproduce locally with minimal runner. i see the same flip when the runtime prefetches KV then detects a different preferred tile size.
Toni: two orthogonal issues: 1) bucketizer uses seq_len buckets only, 2) autotuner has a tiny hysteresis window so it flips quickly on noisy warmup. both cause thrash.
Maya: proposal: include head_dim mod 8/16 in bucket key and increase hysteresis on causal path decisions. also add a metric to trace kernel switches per request.
Sam: agree. add a small backoff before a kernel switch for causal requests that hold KV cache — maybe only evaluate after 2 tokens when microbatch=1.
Liam: quick patch i tested: -> bucket_key = floor(seq_len/32), head_bucket = head_dim if head_dim < 32 else 32, key=(bucket_key, head_bucket). reduces flips for head_dim 22/30. p95 down 30% in synthetic.
Maya: nice. can you open a PR with the bucket change + metric? label perf/regression.
Sam: also add a unit test that simulates kv warmup latency and asserts no kernel switch within first 3 tokens for causal=true and microbatch=1.
Infra-bot: perf-job #452 finished: regression check baseline vs branch=kernel-bucket-branch -> baseline p95=78ms, branch p95=52ms :thumbsup:
Toni: lovely, lets land the bucket change and follow up with a tuning job across SM80/86/90. watch out for head_dim multiples like 14 and 18 that sometimes map to the same head_bucket.
Maya: noted. i'll schedule a cross-arch sweep and add a dashboard panel for kernel-switch rate per model.
Sam: great. tagging this thread for the rollout plan. thanks all. :rocket:
